general_notes.general_notes:
This study is part of a programmatic research effort by the authors, explicitly extending their previous GMV normative modeling work (Segal et al. 2023, Nat Neurosci 26:1613-1629) to white matter using the same clinical sample (25 sites, 14 datasets, 1,465 HC, 1,294 cases). Final sample derived from initial 3,746 individuals after systematic exclusions totaling 885 participants (exclusion rate ~23.6%). Study approved by Monash University Research Ethics Committee (Project ID: 23534) and local ethics committees at each contributing site. Data processing conducted using Multi-modal Australian ScienceS Imaging and Visualization Environment (MASSIVE). Full dataset listing includes: ABIDE I (70) with 9 sites, ABIDE II (71) with 2 sites, ASRB (72) with 4 sites, FEMS (73), MON (74), IMpACT-NL (78), KANMDD (80), MITASD (81,82), OCDPG (75), RUSMDD (83,84), SPAINOCD (76), TOP15 (79), WASHASD (85,86), YoDA (77). HCP dataset used for independent tractography (150 unrelated HC, 71M, ages 21-35). Previous version published as preprint on bioRxiv: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.08.04.606523v1. Parcellation: Schaefer 100-region 7-network cortical parcellation + Tian Subcortical Atlas Scale II 32-region parcellation = 132 total regions. Alternative 20-network parcellation also tested (17 cortical + 3 subcortical). Extensive supplementary analyses provided: Tables S1-S8 (demographics, SVM site classification, deviation burden at multiple thresholds/scales) and Figures S1-S9 (model performance metrics, overlap distributions at multiple scales for negative and positive deviations). Study demonstrates methodological rigor through: multiple threshold sensitivity analyses, cross-validation of site effect removal, systematic quality control with quantified exclusions, and validation of findings across different spatial scales and analytical approaches.

- study_objective: "To characterize interindividual variability in person-specific white matter volume (WMV) deviations across 1294 cases diagnosed with one of 6 psychiatric disorders and to determine the degree to which spatially heterogeneous deviations may accumulate within common white matter pathways, connections tied to individual brain regions, or spatially extended brain networks."

- quality_checking_detail: "Multiple exclusion criteria applied: participants aged <18 or >64 years excluded (N=346); lacking clinical/demographic data excluded (N=53); T1-weighted MRI preprocessing failures excluded (N=63); failed manual QC excluded (N=53); failed automated QC excluded (N=153); sites with <10 individuals per group/sex excluded (N=217). Total excluded: 885 participants. Rank correlations indicated scan quality (measured by CAT12's IQR) was weakly associated with extreme deviation burden for cases (rho=0.07, p=.02), but not for HCtest (rho=-0.04, p=.55). Balanced accuracy scores from SVM site classification ranged 49.71-58.53% across all sites, indicating successful removal of residual site effects."
- site_effect_handling: "Model-based"
- site_effect_handling_detail: "Scan site included as a covariate in the warped Bayesian linear regression normative model. The model was evaluated for efficacy in partitioning site-related variance using linear support vector machines (SVM) with four different kernels (linear, sigmoid, radial basis function, polynomial). Balanced accuracy scores close to chance-level (50%) indicated that resulting deviations were not contaminated by residual site effects. Balanced accuracy scores ranged between 49.71% and 58.53% across all sites, confirming both linear and non-linear site effects were adequately addressed. Training set stratified by site: 90% of controls from each site or all controls if site N<30."

- response_variable: "White matter volume (WMV) estimated voxelwise using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) of T1-weighted anatomical MRI. Normalized segmented white matter images were modulated and spatially smoothed with 8mm FWHM Gaussian kernel. Mean image from all normalized unmodulated white matter maps was generated and voxels with tissue probability ≥0.2 retained."

- predictor_effects: "Age modeled with B-spline basis expansion to capture non-linear effects. Likelihood warping used to model non-Gaussian and heteroscedastic imaging phenotypes. Scan site included as covariate (fixed effect). Sex included as covariate."

- deviation_metric: "Z-score with cluster-based thresholding. Extreme deviations defined as clusters of ≥10 contiguous voxels with deviation scores |z|>2.6 (p<.005). Separate analyses for positive (z>2.6) and negative (z<-2.6) deviations. Deviation burden score: total number of extreme deviation voxels identified per person. Alternative thresholds tested: z<-1.96, z<-1.65 with cluster sizes of 10 or 50 voxels. Overlap maps: proportion of individuals showing extreme deviation in each voxel. Dysconnection overlap matrices: fraction of participants whose WMV deviation intersected specific white matter tracts (8,646 tracts linking 132 regions). Region-scale: proportion of people with at least one affected connection attached to each region. Network-scale: proportion of individuals with at least one extreme deviation in any region of each of 10 functional networks (7 cortical + 3 subcortical)."
- association_analysis: "Case-control differences evaluated using non-parametric permutation testing with 10,000 permutations. For each voxel/edge/region/network, p-values calculated as proportion of null values exceeding observed difference. Tails of null distribution (p<0.10) approximated using generalized Pareto distribution (Winkler et al. 2016) implemented in PALM alpha116 software for arbitrarily high precision inference. FDR correction (Benjamini & Hochberg 1995) applied at pFDR<.05, two-tailed. Mann-Whitney U tests used to compare median extreme deviation burden scores between clinical groups and HCtest (p<.05, one-tailed). Separate analyses conducted for positive and negative deviations at four spatial scales: voxel, tract (connection), region, and network. Multiple threshold sensitivity analyses performed (z thresholds: -2.6, -1.96, -1.65; cluster sizes: 10, 50 voxels; tract weight thresholds: 50%, 75%)."
- key_findings_brief: "WMV deviations showed high voxelwise heterogeneity across all psychiatric disorders (same voxel affected in <8% of individuals with same diagnosis), with lower prevalence than previously observed gray matter deviations; for ASD and SCZ specifically, heterogeneous deviations aggregated into common tracts, regions, and networks affecting up to 69% of individuals."
- key_findings_detailed: "Voxel-scale heterogeneity: Maximum voxel overlap never exceeded 5% for negative deviations across all groups (Table 2). For negative deviations, 21.56% of HCtest showed at least one extreme deviation; for cases: OCD 13.17%, ADHD 16.34%, MDD 19.88%, BP 20.18%, ASD 34.16%, SCZ 35.77%. ASD and SCZ showed significantly higher median negative deviation burden than HCtest (p<.001). Only small isolated areas (<1% of WMV voxels) showed greater overlap in ASD, MDD, SCZ that did not survive FDR correction (pFDR<.05). For positive deviations, 60.59% of HCtest showed extremes; cases ranged from 50.93% (MDD) to 71.78% (ASD). ASD showed higher median positive deviation burden (p=.001). Tract-scale: Maximum overlap ranged from 4.19% (OCD) to 15.40% (SCZ), vs 8.18% in HCtest. ASD showed greater overlap in tracts connecting visual areas and amygdala; SCZ showed greater overlap in somatomotor-thalamic connections (pFDR<.05). Region-scale: Maximum overlap ranged from 8.98% (OCD) to 33.42% (SCZ), vs 14.87% in HCtest. ASD and SCZ showed significantly greater overlap in 86% and 91% of regions, respectively (pFDR<.05). Network-scale: Overlap ranged from 10.18% (OCD: somatomotor, dorsal attention, salience/ventral attention, frontoparietal) to 35.25% (SCZ: dorsal attention, basal ganglia), vs maximum 19.70% in HCtest (dorsal attention, basal ganglia). ASD and SCZ showed greater overlap in all 10 networks (pFDR<.05); OCD showed less overlap in 9/10 networks vs controls (pFDR<.05). No significant differences for ADHD, BP, or MDD at network scale. Fewer than 36% showed negative WMV extremes compared to 76% for GMV in prior study; >61% showed positive WMV extremes. Results consistent across multiple threshold sensitivity analyses (z=-1.96, -1.65; cluster sizes 10, 50; tract thresholds 50%, 75%)."
- key_limitations: "1. VBM-based WMV quantification using Jacobian of nonlinear warp field does not account for white matter's fibrous orientation dependence (changes perpendicular vs. along fiber orientations have different functional impacts). 2. Diffusion MRI tractography limitations: struggles with complex fiber architecture (crossing, branching, turning fibers), partial volume effects, elevated false positives and negatives (validated by tract-tracing comparisons in nonhuman primates), different tractography algorithms show varying sensitivities to errors. 3. DSM-based diagnostic categories are clinical heuristics that do not necessarily define biological entities, with documented limitations including pervasive comorbidity and within-group clinical heterogeneity; focus on syndromes/symptoms cutting across diagnostic boundaries may yield more precise mappings. 4. Group differences in total deviation burden can drive differences in group overlap, complicating inferences about specific targeting of connections/regions/networks; unlike GMV studies with established null models, WMV analyses currently lack such methods, preventing determination of whether overlaps reflect deviation burden differences vs. selective targeting. 5. Study cannot distinguish whether observed overlaps reflect genuine functional consequences or methodological artifacts. 6. Reliance on single imaging modality (structural MRI) rather than multimodal approaches. 7. Cross-sectional design prevents assessment of developmental trajectories or longitudinal changes."
- application_notes: "Authors emphasize extreme voxelwise heterogeneity challenges traditional group-mean approaches, with group-level case-control difference maps likely masking considerable within-group variability. For ASD and SCZ, heterogeneous voxel-level deviations aggregate at coarser spatial scales (tracts, regions, networks), potentially explaining both phenotypic variability (from heterogeneous locations) and phenotypic similarities (from aggregation within common systems) within diagnostic categories. This aggregation pattern was not observed in ADHD, BP, MDD, or OCD, suggesting WMV aberrations may be less pronounced in these conditions. The study extends previous GMV work (Segal et al. 2023, Nat Neurosci) using same sample, revealing WMV deviations are relatively rarer than GMV deviations. Positive WMV deviations more common than negative but biological vs. methodological interpretation unclear; more flexible normative models (Fraza et al. 2021, Dinga et al. 2021) may help address this. Findings support evidence of widespread connectivity changes in ASD and SCZ, consistent with reports of high comorbidity and overlaps in genetics, neuroimaging, clinical signs, and cognitive features between these conditions. For OCD, all networks less likely implicated than controls, potentially reflecting lower total WMV deviation burden; findings consistent with recent evidence that altered structural connectivity unlikely drives observed functional dysregulations in OCD. Future work should: (1) use registration tailored to white matter combined with tractography for greater specificity, (2) focus on symptom dimensions cutting across diagnostic boundaries rather than DSM categories, (3) develop methods to distinguish deviation burden effects from selective targeting, (4) apply multimodal approaches, (5) use harmonized transdiagnostic clinical protocols measuring diverse symptom dimensions."
